repo.description:
### Summary
SeaweedFS fails open on unsupported S3 bucket-policy condition operators. An unauthenticated attacker can bypass a nonmatching condition and read private objects; an explicit empty-permission anonymous identity can also permit writes and deletion.


### Details
Policy validation accepts unknown operators. GetConditionEvaluator returns an error for StringEqualsIgnoreCase, but EvaluateConditions skips the error and ultimately returns true, making the conditional Allow unconditional: [source](https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs/blob/d997fba1575583a89cf0cc50dc0150642286c86d/weed/s3api/policy_engine/conditions.go#L643-L755)

### PoC
On SeaweedFS 4.46, create a private object and apply a wildcard-principal s3:GetObject policy conditioned on StringEquals: {"aws:username":"alice"}. An anonymous GET returns 403. Change only StringEquals to StringEqualsIgnoreCase, reapply the policy, and repeat the same GET: it returns 200 with the exact private object bytes. Restoring StringEquals restores the 403. Full runnable commands are in the linked local draft.


### Impact
Unauthenticated confidentiality bypass affecting private bucket inventory and objects: 7.5 High. With an explicit anonymous identity configured with actions: [], testing also reproduced unauthenticated LIST, GET, PUT, and DELETE, reaching Critical impact.
repo.summary: Unsupported S3 bucket-policy conditions make Allow statements unconditional
